_provenance._why: JSON has no comments and a tuned number without its provenance is how the next reader learns to copy it. Every value below that is not structural carries how it was MEASURED and what would make it wrong. Keys starting with _ are documentation; task.py ignores them.

'T' -- SPEC.md section 6's EXAMPLE value, which shipped -- scores 686 first-party hits, and the first id it mints, T1, is already the set-engine correctness theorem (162 first-party occurrences in 33 files; formal/ARCHITECTURE.md:138, formal/CORRESPONDENCE.md:205). _provenance.min_tasks_parsed: MEASURED: written by migrate.py as the exact number of task files it just wrote, and re-derivable any time with `task.py counts`. ZERO HEADROOM, the way formal/verify.sh sets MIN_CONF_ALL / MIN_TESTS_ALL. It shipped at 5 -- SPEC.md section 6's example again -- which left 94 files of headroom: `rm -rf tasks/closed` destroyed 57 files (58% of the corpus) and lint still printed 'clean (10 checks, 42 task file(s) parsed)', exit 0. A RAW TOTAL and not an open/closed pair, because total is the only quantity that cannot legitimately fall (files are never deleted, close is a MOVE), while open falls on every close and closed falls on every reopen; a zero-headroom floor on either half would redden on correct use. Growth is handled by check_min_parsed's second assertion, an independent per-directory recount, not by padding this number. Adding tasks is free; RAISING this is a deliberate reviewed edit; LOWERING it to make a run green is the defect it exists to catch. TWO checks now ride this one value: task.py lint check_min_parsed, and handoff_lint.py, which DERIVES its id floor from this key rather than restating it (it used to carry its own copy, and two zero-headroom floors on the same quantity in two files is ZT-P3-5 waiting to happen). Raising it here raises both; lowering it lowers both. RATCHETED 99 -> 149 on 2026-08-21b: file_backlog.py filed all 50 rows of filing-plan.json through task.py (48 open + 2 closed-on-arrival records), and `task.py counts` then measured 149 parsed / 149 *.md on disk. The raise is the point -- adding tasks is free, but leaving the floor at 99 would have handed the corpus 50 files of fresh headroom, which is exactly the state that let `rm -rf tasks/closed` print `clean`. No label vocabulary widening was needed: all 50 items used formal/perf/docs/infra as already declared. RATCHETED 149 -> 150 on 2026-08-21c: TK51 was filed at 2026-08-21c (COVERAGE.md's 'Dropped, with reasons' J-26) and the floor was not raised with it, so the corpus carried one file of headroom and test_task.py's test_shipped_config_is_measured_not_an_example was RED (that suite is tracked as tests/test_tasktool.py since 2026-08-29d; path corrected, the 2026-08-21c numbers around it are historical and stand) ('floor 149 vs 150 files on disk'). Found by the schema-13 pass, which did not create the gap and does not close it by lowering anything: `task.py counts` measured 150 parsed / 150 *.md and 150 is what it prints as the value to paste. One file of headroom is the same defect as ninety-four, only cheaper to miss. RATCHETED 150 -> 153 on 2026-08-29d (150 -> 152 for accumulated growth, then -> 153 when TT-1 was filed in the same session): the corpus had grown to 152 while the floor sat at 150, i.e. two files of headroom re-accumulated exactly as the growth paragraph above predicts; `task.py counts` measured 152 parsed / 152 *.md on disk and printed 152 as the value to paste. Same session added tasks/BANNER.md and tasks/README.md, which are NOT tasks and are excluded by exact name at the top level (task.py::NON_TASK_MD) from BOTH scanners -- Store.md_paths and the independent recount disk_md_count -- so they do not inflate this number and check 10's recount still agrees. That exclusion is shared as a CONSTANT and duplicated as a WALK on purpose: a blind scanner is still caught, and the two halves cannot disagree about the banner's filename.
_provenance.stale_days: JUDGEMENT, inside a MEASURED band -- there is no way to derive it exactly, and the honest thing is to say so. Lower bound 7: the longest observed gap between two working days in this repo is 6 (docs/history/*.md, 30 distinct dated days across 2026-07-08..2026-08-21, gaps p50=1 p90=3 max=6), so any threshold at or below 6 flags rows because NOBODY WORKED THE REPO rather than because the row was neglected -- a false positive in the instrument, not a finding. Upper bound 23: the oldest `moved` in the open corpus is 23 days, so 24+ can never fire on today's tree and a warning that cannot fire is not a warning. 14 is chosen inside [7, 23] as roughly ten working sessions at the measured rate of 30 working days per 44 calendar days (0.68/day): ten sessions that all declined to touch a NOW/NEXT row IS neglect, three is just a week. Today it flags exactly 1 of 42 open rows and 0 of 3 NOW/NEXT rows. Re-derive with measure_stale.py if the cadence changes.
